The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic tangent function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{artanh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\sqrt{7}\operatorname{artanh}⁡(\sqrt{3}\,x)) \\  & =-\sqrt{7}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{artanh}⁡(\sqrt{3}\,x)) \\  & =-\sqrt{7}\cdot \frac{1}{1-{(\sqrt{3}\,x)}^{2}}\cdot {(\sqrt{3}\,x)}^{′} \\  & =-\sqrt{7}\cdot \frac{1}{1-3{x}^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{3} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{21}}{3{x}^{2}-1}.\end{aligned}
$$
